analysis:
The only changed line is docs/provider/cli-reference.md:1025, a documentation bullet under `darkbloom status`. It says App Attest serving authorization can stay visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice requires a matching fresh coordinator decision. It adds a pointer to ../reference/provider-authorization.md. No code, config, protocol, or key/credential handling changes. The surrounding unchanged text (logout, revocation, drain, add-on hold, Autopilot, prefix-cache posture) was read as context and not treated as new behavior.

The new sentence matches the threat model's separation of authorization from advice. It is consistent with T-053 (a stale authorization must not outlive revocation, so the lease display is not a grant), with T-057 (premature MDM removal stranding a provider), and with T-052 (a label must not be mistaken for permission). It does not widen the trust claim. It also makes no claim that a visible lease means current coordinator authority.

Open question for integration: the referenced provider-authorization.md was not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm the link target exists or matches the stated semantics. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. No evidence of a new attack surface, an invalidated assumption, or a need to update the threat model from this change.
